title: Who sets the rules of the internet? The decisions most users never notice
body:
The multistakeholder approach plays an important role in internet governance, bringing governments, technology companies, technical communities and civil society into decision-making processes.

For example, ICANN coordinates key functions of the domain name system, international technical communities develop standards, governments establish legal requirements, and technology companies implement specific solutions in their products. [...] However, the growth of a national technology industry does not automatically translate into a proportionate influence on international standard-setting.

A country can develop successful digital products while remaining dependent on rules and infrastructure largely shaped beyond its borders.

Another challenge is policy continuity.

Inconsistent policies and weak institutions can mean that progress made under one government stalls when political leadership changes. [...] Sometimes countries have to revisit stages they have already completed.

This is particularly important for international digital governance. Participation in standards development can take years, while shifting government priorities can interrupt the accumulation of expertise and the implementation of decisions already made.

Influence over global digital rules also depends on a country’s ability to build stable institutions capable of representing national interests across political cycles.

Much of the Internet operates through technical standards and coordination systems developed by international organizations rather than through agreements negotiated exclusively by governments.
